steps.title: Key Point
steps.body: Sentence variety is essential for AO6 marks. Writing that uses only one sentence type feels monotonous and shows limited technical control. Varied sentences create rhythm, pace, and impact.

steps.title: Short Sentences = Impact
steps.body: A short sentence after several long ones stands out. It hits the reader harder because it's surrounded by more complex structures.

steps.title: FANBOYS - Coordinating Conjunctions
steps.body: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So

steps.title: Subordinating Conjunctions
steps.body: Because, although, when, while, if, since, before, after, unless, as, though, whereas

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What is the difference between a simple, compound, and complex sentence? | Name three ways to vary sentence openings. | When would you use short sentences in your writing?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Simple = one clause (one subject, one verb). Compound = two or more independent clauses joined by coordinating conjunctions (and, but, or). Complex = one independent clause and one or more dependent c | Start with: adverbs (Slowly, ...), -ing verbs (Running, ...), prepositions (Across the field, ...), connectives (However, ...), time phrases (Moments later, ...), subordinate clauses (Although tired,  | For dramatic impact, to build tension, to speed up pace, to emphasise a key moment, to create contrast with longer sentences, for action scenes.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Plan for variety - consciously use different sentence types Save short sentences for key moments of impact Use complex sentences to add depth and detail Vary your sentence openers - avoid repetitive patterns Read your work aloud - listen for rhythm and flow Use sentence length to control pace intentionally Check: do you have a mix of simple, compound, and complex? Mark scheme specifically rewards "varied sentences"
